pull.title: MINOR: Fix race in StreamsGroupWarmupTaskIntegrationTest
pull.body:
The test sampled the thread metadata for a standby task to detect the
warm-up. The metadata shows it only until the promotion, so a test
thread stalled for about two heartbeat intervals missed it and timed
out. Record the warm-up's start and its promotion through a
StandbyUpdateListener instead.

Follow up to https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23608

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

review_comments.body: The pointer to warmupChangelogs doesn't really justify this. The restore listener never sees the warm-up (as the comment further down says), so the warm-up count says nothing about how often onBatchRestored fires. What we actually expect is that it never fires (the assertEquals(-1L, ...) at the end). Maybe just say that here?

issue.title: MINOR: Add streams group protocol integration test for warm-up tasks

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
This ports the scale-out warm-up scenario from
HighAvailabilityTaskAssignorIntegrationTest, which exercises the classic
protocol's client-side HighAvailabilityTaskAssignor, to the streams
group protocol. Under the streams group protocol, warm-up derivation
happens broker-side via an AssignmentRefiner, which defaults to a no-op
implementation, so the test enables the real AssignmentRefinerImpl
explicitly to get coverage of the actual warm-up behavior against a live
cluster with real KafkaStreams clients, which did not exist before.

The test proves the same property as the original: when a stateful app
scales out, the new instance is first handed a warm-up task rather than
being promoted to active immediately, and is only promoted once its
local state has caught up, at which point the promotion happens with
zero real state restoration because the warm-up's state is reused
directly.

Two mechanisms from the original test don't carry over and needed
replacements. There is no client-side assignment-listener equivalent
under the streams group protocol, since that callback is wired into the
classic protocol's client-side assignor, so warm-up assignment and later
promotion are instead detected by polling
KafkaStreams.metadataForLocalThreads() for a task moving from the
standby set into the active set. On the target-assignment side, the
streams group protocol currently only ships the sticky assignor, which
balances active task load across processes rather than doing plain round
robin, but its load-balancing quota math still forces one of the two
tasks in this scenario onto the new, empty instance's target assignment,
which is exactly the mismatch the refiner needs in order to stage a
warm-up. So the test works with the sticky assignor as is, and does not
need to wait for a more round-robin-like assignor.

The rack-aware parameterization from the original test was dropped,
since the streams group protocol's sticky assignor has no rack-aware
placement logic today, so that axis would not exercise anything
meaningful. The in-memory versus persistent store parameterization was
kept, since it is a pure client-side choice orthogonal to the group
protocol.

### Test plan

- Ran both parameterized variants locally against a live 3-broker
embedded KRaft cluster; both pass.
- Confirmed via logs that the new instance is assigned a warm-up task
before promotion (`warm-up tasks {0_1}`, no active task), and that the
state-restore listener reports zero restored records at promotion time.
- `./gradlew spotlessApply checkstyleMain checkstyleTest` is clean.

Reviewers: Bill Bejeck <bbejeck@apache.org>
